vocab.definition: measures the environmental impact of a product.
the resources extracted to make the product.
energy/water used making and using the product.
what happens at the end — landfill or recycling.

misconceptions.wrong: An LCA only looks at making a product.
misconceptions.right: It covers the whole life from raw materials to disposal.
Some impacts are hard to measure, so judgements are made.
Collecting and reprocessing also use energy.

infoPanels.title: FOUR LCA STAGES
workedSteps: Consider energy, water, resources and waste at each stage.

questions.text: State what a life cycle assessment measures. [1 mark]
List the four stages considered in an LCA. [2 marks]
Explain why a plastic bag may have a lower LCA impact than a paper bag in some areas. [2 marks]
Explain why an LCA is not entirely objective. [2 marks]
Complete the sentence using the word bank. [2 marks]
questions.secondaryText: An LCA runs from ______ all the way through to ______.

questions.text: Suggest how a company could use an LCA to improve a product. [1 mark]

footer.tip: An LCA covers raw materials, manufacture, use AND disposal.
footer.thinkPrompt: Why might companies be tempted to present LCA data in a biased way?
